column1: # nixos/tests/registry.tsv — every suite this repository can run, declared.
# WHY A FILE INSTEAD OF AN ARRAY IN run.sh
# Three lists had to be kept in step by hand: the suites to run, the files to
# shellcheck, and the nix flake outputs. They drifted. The clearest drift was
# silent: the agent-operations lane landed with its own run.sh, that run.sh was
# never added to the top-level list, and so its suites simply did not run —
# while the overall runner still printed "all checks passed". A check that is
# registered nowhere cannot report that it was skipped.
# So registration is data, and discovery checks it. Every executable suite
# under tests/ must appear here; one that does not is a FAILURE, not an
# omission. That inverts the default: the safe state is a loud error, and
# adding a suite without registering it cannot pass.
# COLUMNS (tab-separated):
#   lane      which PR/area owns this suite; the lane is the unit of ownership
#   path      relative to nixos/ (the flake root), e.g. tests/... or config/...
#   scope     fast   pure bash / cargo, no nix, no privileges, < ~10s
#             eval   needs `nix` to evaluate configurations
#             kvm    needs KVM and a full NixOS build; NOT run by run.sh
#   kind      shell  a standalone bash suite
#             lane   a run.sh that aggregates its own sub-suites
#             cargo  a crate whose `cargo test` is the suite
# `kvm` is declared but never executed by run.sh. It is listed so that
# maintenance-vm.nix is accounted for somewhere and cannot quietly vanish from
# the picture; it is run with `nix build`, and run.sh says so when asked.
